root_cause: Only 1 of 71,641 CPU functional tests failed: a single ACL-backed ConvertCPULayerTest_7D_Dynamic case asserted the selected primitive implementation type was 'acl_i32' but the runtime reported 'unknown_i32'. This is the same recurring ACL (ARM Compute Library) primitive-selection flakiness previously observed across ConvertCPULayerTest, MatMulLayerCPUTest, MatMulDecompressConvertTest, and PoolingLayerCPUTest on ARM64 (patterns 76751669c7a78fcd, 0de8f57e3fb03230, eb0b94c864ee1a85), where ACL's kernel-selection heuristics intermittently fail to register a primitive type for certain input shapes/precisions depending on runner load or threading, independent of the code under test. PR #38389 changes only src/common/transformations/.../restore_traced_batch.* (a new smart_reshape transformation) and has no relation to the CPU plugin's ACL dispatch code or ConvertCPULayerTest, confirming the failure is unrelated to the PR diff.
reproduction_steps: Build CPU plugin for ARM64 (Ubuntu 22.04 cross-compilation) and run: ov_cpu_func_tests --gtest_filter=*smoke_ConvertCPULayerTest_7D_Dynamic/ConvertCPULayerTest.CompareWithRefs*inputPRC=i32*primitive=acl* repeatedly; the ACL primType assertion in cpu_test_utils.cpp:248 fails intermittently depending on ACL kernel/primitive selection for i32 Convert inputs.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed CPU functional tests job; this is known flaky ACL primitive-selection behavior unrelated to PR #38389's diff.

Track the recurring ACL primType mismatch (unknown_* vs acl_*/undef_* vs acl_*) across Convert/MatMul/Pooling CPU layer tests as a single ARM64 CPU-plugin flakiness ticket and consider adding a bounded retry or diagnostic logging around the primTypeCheck assertion in cpu_test_utils.cpp.
No action required on PR #38389 itself - the failure is confined to an unrelated ARM64/ACL CPU functional test.
prevention_strategies: Add a short internal retry (or gtest repeat) for primTypeCheck specifically for ACL-backed primitives in cpu_test_utils.cpp, since ACL kernel/primitive selection can legitimately vary by runtime/thread count; log both selected and expected primitive type on mismatch to speed up triage without blocking unrelated merge-queue PRs.
historical_context: This is the 6th recorded ACL primType-mismatch signature variant since July 2026 (siblings: 76751669c7a78fcd, 0de8f57e3fb03230, cb7d14bccc236de4, eb0b94c864ee1a85 count=4, and the earlier Code-Issue-labeled 75ebbbb77b09e3b0 for the identical i32/acl_i32 text which turned out, on repeated unrelated-PR occurrences of the broader pattern family, to be the same recurring ACL flakiness rather than a genuine code defect).
